summary: Frontend-only verification of Exit Engine data-consistency fixes (P0 launch). PARTIAL PASS: (1) Code review confirms the single-source-of-truth architecture is correctly wired — describeActiveExit() in /app/frontend/src/lib/exitConfig.js is imported by BOTH ExitEngineWorkflow.jsx (line 9, used in ActiveExitCard at line 332) AND RiskMonitorPanel.jsx (line 7, used at line 53), so the two web cards CANNOT disagree by construction — for fixed_pct the rows are Take-Profit target + Stop-Loss (never Trail multiplier), fixing the previously reported inconsistency. (2) Web testIDs present as advertised: active-exit-card, active-exit-type, active-exit-edit, active-exit-val-* on the Exit Engine home step 1; rm-active-exit + rm-active-name on Risk Monitor. Mobile testIDs ee-active-exit, ee-active-name, ee-edit-current, ee-modify-global, ee-set-target_pct, ee-set-stop_pct, ee-deploy, ee-subtab-risk, rm-active-exit, rm-active-name are all present in workspace.tsx. (3) editActive() in ExitEngineWorkflow.jsx:80-85 correctly reads describeActiveExit(saved), sets scope + method, and jumps to Configure step 3 — the Edit/Modify button routes into the modify flow pre-set to the active method. (4) Web card LIVE VERIFIED in browser once (screenshot /tmp/w_ee_home.png): initial 'Universal Exit Engine' with Trail multiplier 2x / Breakeven arm 1.6% / Hard stop-loss 2.2% (native branch of describeActiveExit — correct). (5) BACKEND fixes verified via curl on the shared backend: PUT /api/settings with fixed_target_pct=7, stop_loss_pct=3.2 persists correctly; a subsequent PUT with BOTH keys set to null returns 200 and DOES NOT overwrite the values (still 7/3.2 after) — fix (C) drops-nulls confirmed working; switch to atr_trailing works; reset to native/3.0/2.2 done at end. LIMITATIONS: The full end-to-end web UI deploy click-path (Modify Global → Fixed% → type 7/3.2 → Deploy) could not be completed because the post-login OnboardingPipeline 'ENTER ANANTA' finale modal became sticky in this test environment and neither testid-based click, force-click, nor JS-dispatched .click() on [data-testid="onboarding-enter"] dismissed it after 3 attempts (per Loop Prevention) — see context_for_next_testing_agent. Full mobile flow was NOT executed in this iteration to conserve budget; the mobile-specific NumRow NaN chain identified in iter78 should still be spot-checked once web modal issue is unblocked. DB left in clean default state (native / 3.0 / 2.2 / 1.6 / 0.9).

integration_issues.issue: After OWNER LOGIN the OnboardingPipeline finale modal ('ENTER ANANTA' / 'Your trading operating system is ready') can become sticky — clicks on [data-testid="onboarding-enter"] (Playwright click force=True AND direct JS el.click()) did not fire onClose in this session, blocking automated UI testing of Exit Engine deploy flow. Likely re-render race with auth/onboarded state. Suggest: guard OnboardingPipeline so it does NOT re-open after localStorage 'ananta_onboarded'=1, or expose a more robust dismissal handler. Not user-facing when localStorage is already primed, but a repeatable QA blocker.

action_items: MEDIUM (web): make OnboardingPipeline reliably dismissable — either don't remount on auth state change once ananta_onboarded=1, or make onboarding-enter/onboarding-skip idempotent (currently blocks automated E2E test runs).

LOW (mobile DRY): /app/mobile/app/(tabs)/workspace.tsx:48 duplicates describeActiveExit() logic byte-for-byte from /app/frontend/src/lib/exitConfig.js. Content matches (verified) so parity is preserved today, but any future edit to one and not the other will silently re-open the exact inconsistency bug this iteration was chartered to fix. Extract to a shared TS module (e.g. /app/mobile/lib/exitConfig.ts) and keep the two in lock-step.

RETEST (mobile — carry-over from iter78): confirm the workspace.tsx setF NaN-guard + NumRow useEffect Number.isFinite guard + deploy() finite-value validation are in place and that clear-and-retype in ee-set-target_pct/ee-set-stop_pct no longer produces a NaN → null PUT body. Backend now drops nulls (verified), so worst-case damage is contained, but the mobile UX should still commit typed values.
critical_code_review_comments: /app/frontend/src/lib/exitConfig.js — clean single source of truth, describeActiveExit correctly branches on exit_method_pref: fixed_pct → Take-Profit target + Stop-Loss (fixes the RiskMonitor showing Trail/Breakeven/HardStop when Fixed% was active). atr_trailing/chandelier → Trail arm + Trail distance + Hard stop-loss. Fallback (native) → Trail multiplier + Breakeven arm + Hard stop-loss. All numeric fields defensively coerced via num()/fallback.
/app/frontend/src/components/ExitEngineWorkflow.jsx:80-85 editActive() — correctly derives scope+method from describeActiveExit(saved) and jumps to Configure step. Good.

/app/frontend/src/components/ExitEngineWorkflow.jsx:127-151 deploy() — for method.id === 'fixed_pct' sends BOTH stop_loss_pct AND fixed_target_pct in the patch (line 132). Good; matches what backend expects.

/app/frontend/src/components/ExitEngineWorkflow.jsx:63-74 savedCfgFor() — merges last-deployed values over method defaults so re-opening the flow shows what the user actually saved. Persistence path structurally intact.

/app/frontend/src/components/RiskMonitorPanel.jsx:53 — const active = describeActiveExit(s). Card at line 69 uses active.typeLabel + active.rows. This is the exact same computation the Exit Engine home card uses, so the two cards are provably identical for any given settings object.
/app/mobile/app/(tabs)/workspace.tsx:48-67 — mobile has its OWN describeActiveExit (duplicate of web). Bytes match today; risk is future divergence. Extract to a shared module.

Backend PUT /api/settings null-drop behaviour verified end-to-end: sending {"fixed_target_pct":null,"stop_loss_pct":null} returned 200 and left the previously-saved 7.0/3.2 intact. This closes the iter78 self-poisoning failure mode where a bad client write could 500 the entire settings surface.

success_rate.backend: n/a (frontend-only ask; but backend PUT-null-drop spot-checked via curl and PASSES)
success_rate.frontend: web: code-level fixes VERIFIED correct; runtime UI deploy flow BLOCKED by onboarding modal issue in this test session. Mobile: not exercised this iteration.

seed_data_creation: Temporarily set exit_method_pref=fixed_pct / fixed_target_pct=7 / stop_loss_pct=3.2 via authenticated PUT /api/settings to test the null-drop backend fix. Restored to defaults at end: exit_method_pref=native, fixed_target_pct=3.0, stop_loss_pct=2.2, trail_arm_pct=1.6, trail_distance_pct=0.9. Verified via GET.
context_for_next_testing_agent: To reproduce the modal issue: fresh incognito, goto /, localStorage.setItem('ananta_onboarded','1'), click OWNER LOGIN → LOG IN, wait ~4s for the OnboardingPipeline 'Welcome to Ananta / PROVISIONING' animation to complete, click [data-testid="onboarding-enter"] — in this session the click event fired but the modal did not unmount (screenshots /tmp/w_ee_fixed.png attempts). Workaround that worked ONCE: click a button:has-text('CLOSE') at top-right of the modal, then button:has-text('Continue to Cockpit') on the 'Coming Soon' promo modal, then click bottom-nav 'EXIT ENGINE' text. Once past both modals, the Exit Engine home renders and testids resolve: active-exit-card / active-exit-type / active-exit-edit / scope-global / wf-next-1 / method-fixed_pct. Backend already accepts fixed_target_pct=7/stop_loss_pct=3.2 and rejects null writes. When you can drive the UI, the two cards WILL agree because they share exitConfig.js. Reset DB via authenticated PUT /api/settings {exit_method_pref:'native', fixed_target_pct:3.0, stop_loss_pct:2.2, trail_arm_pct:1.6, trail_distance_pct:0.9} when done (already reset now).
rca of the issue: This iteration's data-consistency ask has TWO independent proof layers: (a) STATIC — one shared describeActiveExit() is imported by both web cards + duplicated (byte-identical) on mobile, so the RiskMonitor can no longer show Trail/Breakeven when Fixed% is active; verified in code. (b) DYNAMIC — backend correctly persists Fixed% values 7/3.2 AND drops null writes, verified via curl. The user-visible click-path could not be automated end-to-end in this session due to a sticky onboarding-modal race, which is itself a QA-blocker but not the P0 bug this iteration was chartered to fix.
